top.h1: Where was Tenochtitlan, and how big was it?
answer: Tenochtitlan stood on islands and built-up land in western Lake Texcoco, under Mexico City's historic centre, where its
is dug out. It covered about 9 to 14 km², and most
put its people, with Tlatelolco, at 75,000 to 400,000, many near 150,000 to 200,000.
top.strength: Where it lay: known from digs, letters and maps. Its area: estimated, about 9 to 14 km². Its people: guessed, as no count survives.

slot.what: How big Tenochtitlan was, by who gives which figure, and where it lay, by finds under today's Mexico City. The dots are digs and sites on today's streets. No line joins them, because the old shore and the city's edge are not known closely enough to draw.
slot.alt: A chart and a map in two panels. The chart sets the estimates for Tenochtitlan with Tlatelolco side by side, every bar dashed as a guess. Its people run from 60,000 (Lombardo) and 75,000 to 95,000 (Jiménez Martínez) to 360,000 (Borah and Cook) and 560,000 to 700,000 (Soustelle), with Smith at 212,500, and two claims of the 16th century, 60,000 and more than a million, are marked as claims. The map marks digs and sites on today's streets of central Mexico City: the Templo Mayor, the site of Axayácatl's palace, the south-west edge in colonia Tránsito, an old floor in La Lagunilla, and Tlatelolco's landing place and north edge.

paras: Under the historic centre of Mexico City, which grew on and over it. The Mexica, often called the Aztecs, settled about 1325 on an islet in western Lake Texcoco,
. By their own history, their god Huitzilopochtli showed them the place by a sign, an eagle standing on a nopal cactus, and there they founded México-Tenochtitlan. In 2025
announced a memorial marking 700 years of México-Tenochtitlan. Tlatelolco, its sister city, became a fifth quarter after its conquest in 1473,
. The city grew on chinampas, fields built up from the lake bed (see
INAH's Templo Mayor project has dug between calles Argentina and Guatemala since workers found the carved stone of the goddess Coyolxauhqui in 1978 (
). Calle de Tacuba runs on the old western causeway, and the Nacional Monte de Piedad stands where Axayácatl's palace stood (
Hernán Cortés entered the city on 8 November 1519, after meeting Motecuhzoma Xocoyotzin, Moctezuma II, and at the end of June 1520 the Mexica drove his men out (

). In 1521 his men laid siege with "un gran apoyo de Tlaxcala y Texcoco", great support from Tlaxcala and Texcoco. The siege ended on 13 August 1521, when the canoe carrying Cuauhtémoc, the tlatoani (ruler), was taken (
). After the conquest the Indigenous people left the city and died in great numbers, falling from 200,000 to perhaps 50,000, by the estimate of

blocks.nav: How big was Tenochtitlan, and how many people lived there?
blocks.h: How big was Tenochtitlan, and how many people lived there?
paras: About 9 to 14 square kilometres, with 75,000 to 400,000 people, Tlatelolco included, by most modern estimates. No count survives, and Cortés gave no figure,

paras.text: Eloy Jiménez Martínez notes in his review

paras: . Cortés wrote "Es tan grande la ciudad como Sevilla y Córdoba", as large as Seville and Córdoba, and whether he meant either or both is open (
has "or").

Later writers counted houses or householders (vecinos), not people. The so-called Anonymous Conqueror, whose account survives in an Italian version and who called himself a companion of Cortés, gives 60,000 inhabitants ("habitantes"), perhaps householders, and one historian doubted he was there. How many people stood behind one householder is not known: 4.5 by tradition, anywhere from 3 to 7, and a Mexica house often held an extended family.

As gathered by Jiménez Martínez, modern estimates run from Sonia Lombardo's 60,000 (1973) to Charles Gibson's 250,000 to 400,000 (1964) and Jacques Soustelle's 560,000 to 700,000 (1955). Michael E. Smith (2005) gives 212,500 people on 1,365 hectares (
), Jiménez Martínez 75,000 to 95,000 on at most 9.44 km².

He tables Seville (about 1500) at 65,000, Córdoba (about 1509) at 27,806, Paris (about 1500) at 150,000, Venice (about 1558) at 158,000, Constantinople (about 1550) at 500,000, Cuzco (about 1533) at 125,000 and Tzintzuntzan (about 1519) at 30,000.
and Nicolás Sánchez-Albornoz, as Jiménez Martínez quotes him, call Tenochtitlan the largest city in the Americas, though on Jiménez Martínez's estimate Cuzco, as he tables it, would be larger.
It was drained, step by step, to keep the city from flooding. Before the conquest, five lakes filled the basin and joined into one in the rainy season (
). Chalco and Xochimilco were fresh, the other three salty, and together they covered about 600 km² by
The first great drainage canal, the Desagüe, was dug from 1607 by some 40,000 workers but could not drain Lake Texcoco (
). The Gran Canal opened in 1900 (
), and the deep drainage, the Drenaje Profundo, was begun in 1967 (
Today the old lake bed compacts as groundwater is pumped out, and some parts of the city sank about 35 centimetres a year in the 1990s and 2000s (
). Lake Nabor Carrillo is an artificial lake built over part of the old bed (
), and 14,030 hectares at Lake Texcoco have been protected since 2022 (

blocks.nav: What does the map of 1524 show?
blocks.h: What does the map of 1524 show?
paras: Tenochtitlan, in a woodcut printed by Friedrich Peypus in Nuremberg in March 1524, in the Latin edition of Cortés's second letter, with the coast of the Gulf of Mexico in the same woodcut (
). It was "the first picture Europeans had" of the city,

. Its source is not known, and she argues that an Indigenous map lay behind it. Once printed, she adds, it was certainly documentary and also came to support the claim that the conquest was just. Nothing on this page is measured from it.
From digs under the modern city, 16th-century letters and chronicles, and modern estimates of area and density.

INAH's rescue digs show how far the city reached. At Ateponazco in 2015 they found its south-west edge, toward today's Calzada Chabacano. In La Lagunilla in 2022, on the old border with Tlatelolco, they found a Late Postclassic floor (1350 to 1519) only 1.20 metres down (
). And a dig at Eje 2 Norte Manuel González in 2023 and 2024 led INAH to place Tlatelolco's north edge about 300 metres further on, at Calzada San Simón (

subs.h: "Tenochtitlan was the largest city in the world."
paras: It was the largest in the Americas, by Smith and Sánchez-Albornoz. On most estimates, 75,000 to 400,000, it was smaller than Constantinople, which Jiménez Martínez tables at 500,000 about 1550.
It stood on islets and on land built up from the shallow lake bed as chinampas.

subs.h: "The Spaniards drained the lake right after the conquest."
paras: The lakes began to shrink soon after 1521, Arturo Montero says, and he dates their drying out from 1750. The great canals came from 1607 to 1900.
Small waters remain, under 10 km² together by Montero's count, and 14,030 hectares are protected.
